note: Covers the whole lifecycle of running models on constrained hardware, from model design through runtime optimisation. Relevant to our on-device and edge model sections.
title: A Review on Edge Large Language Models: Design, Execution, and Applications
explain_beginner: Large language models are powerful AI systems that understand and generate text, but they require enormous computing power. This paper reviews how researchers are making these models small and efficient enough to run directly on phones, tablets, and other portable devices. The work matters because it enables AI features to work without internet connection, faster responses, and greater privacy for users.
explain_business: This survey maps the technical landscape for running AI language models on edge devices, enabling companies to deliver AI features that work offline, reduce server costs, and improve user privacy. Understanding the design-to-deployment lifecycle helps organizations decide whether on-device AI is feasible for their applications and what technical investments would be required to make it practical.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive survey examines the full pipeline for deploying LLMs on resource-constrained devices. It covers three main stages: designing models for efficiency, implementing pre-deployment optimization strategies, and applying runtime inference techniques. The review synthesizes current techniques for reducing computational and memory demands while addressing hardware diversity in edge environments, identifying architectural innovations and optimization approaches that enable practical on-device deployment.
